Rashi on Niddah 32a:10:1.english: If so - That [Rabbi Meir] is concerned for the minority.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:10:2.english: Our [girls] as well - Let all of them be impure from their cradle.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:11:1.english: "A woman" and "and a woman" - To include a minor [girl], as [the Gemara] explains.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:11:2.english: They separate them - From contact with consecrated items.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:12:1.hebrew: ואשה כי תהיה זבה וגו' - בנדה משתעי קרא, דכתיב (ויקרא ט״ו:י״ט) שבעת ימים תהיה בנדתה:
Rashi on Niddah 32a:12:1.english: And if a woman has an issue, etc. - The verse is speaking of a menstruating woman, as it is written (Leviticus 15:19): "Seven days she shall be in her menstruation."

Rashi on Niddah 32a:13:1.english: And they raised a contradiction: "A woman" - [In the verse:] "And a woman with whom a man shall lie with an emission of semen."

Rashi on Niddah 32a:13:2.hebrew: לביאה - שמטמאה בביאת אדם מגזרת הכתוב, דכתיב וטמאו, ולא משום נוגעת בשכבת זרע הוא, שהרי מגע בית הסתרים הוא, ואינו מטמא:
Rashi on Niddah 32a:13:2.english: For intercourse - That she becomes impure through human intercourse by scriptural decree, as it is written: "And they shall be impure," and it is not because she touches semen, for it is contact in a concealed part [of the body], and does not transmit impurity.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:14:1.hebrew: הלכתא נינהו - לענין נדה בת יום אחד, ולענין ביאה בת ג', דברים הללו הלכה למשה מסיני הם, כדמפרש ואזיל דחדא מינייהו הלכתא:
Rashi on Niddah 32a:14:1.english: They are halakhot - Regarding [the status of] a one-day-old [girl as] a niddah, and regarding intercourse [with a girl] aged three [years] — these matters are a halakha [transmitted] to Moses from Sinai, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain that one of them is a halakha.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:14:2.hebrew: הי קרא והי הלכתא - כלומר, מכדי קרא חדא מינייהו משתמע, הי מינייהו משתמע מקרא בלא הלכתא, והי מינייהו אצטריך הלכתא:
Rashi on Niddah 32a:14:2.english: Which is the verse and which is the halakha - That is to say: Since [only] one of them is inferred from the verse, which of them is inferred from the verse without the halakha, and which of them required the halakha?

Rashi on Niddah 32a:14:3.hebrew: קרא סתמא כתיב - כיון דוי"ו לרבויי אתא, כל שהוא אשה משמע, בת יום אחד. אבל בת ג' לא משמע מיניה טפי מבת ב' או בת ד':
Rashi on Niddah 32a:14:3.english: The verse is written without specification - Since the [letter] vav comes to include, it implies anyone who is [considered] a woman — [even] a one-day-old. But [a girl of] three is not implied by it any more than [a girl of] two or [a girl of] four.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:15:1.hebrew: אלא בת ג' - לענין ביאה הלכתא, דמקרא לא משתמע, ורבנן אסמכתא בעלמא אסמכוה; ובת יום א' לנדה משתמעא מקרא:
Rashi on Niddah 32a:15:1.english: Rather, [a girl] of three [years] - With regard to intercourse, [it is] a halakha [transmitted to Moses from Sinai], for it is not implied from the verse, and the Sages merely supported it as an asmakhta; and a one-day-old [girl] regarding nidda is implied from the verse.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:15:2.hebrew: ומאחר - דביאה בת ג' הלכה למשה מסיני היא, ומקרא לא משתמע, עיקר קרא דוי"ו יתירא למאי אתא:
Rashi on Niddah 32a:15:2.english: And now that - Since [the law regarding] the intercourse of a girl aged three is a halakha transmitted to Moses from Sinai, and is not derived from Scripture, what did the primary [purpose of the] verse with the superfluous vav come [to teach]?

Rashi on Niddah 32a:2:1.hebrew: איש כתוב בפרשה - (דברים כ״ה:ז׳) ואם לא יחפוץ האיש, איש פוטרה בחליצה, ולא קטן. אלא מה טעם אין מיבמין, ויגדלו יחד:
Rashi on Niddah 32a:2:1.english: "Man" is written in the passage - (Deuteronomy 25:7) "And if the man does not want" — an adult man exempts her through ḥalitza, and not a minor. Rather, what is the reason that they may not enter into levirate marriage and grow up together?

Rashi on Niddah 32a:3:1.hebrew: סריס - לאו בר הקמת שם הוא, ואינו מצווה ליבם, וכן אילונית. וכיון דמייבם בלא מצוה, נושא אשת אחיו בחנם, וערוה היא, ובכרת:
Rashi on Niddah 32a:3:1.english: A sexually underdeveloped man - He is not capable of establishing a name [for his brother], and he is not commanded to perform levirate marriage; and likewise a sexually underdeveloped woman [ayalonit]. And since he performs levirate marriage without a mitzvah, he marries his brother's wife gratuitously, and she is a forbidden relative, and [the union is punishable] by excision [karet].

Rashi on Niddah 32a:6:1.english: In Ein Bul - [This is] a place.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:6:2.hebrew: קודם לאמה - יולדת נקבה טובלת לי"ד, ובתה ראתה ליום או ליומים שנולדה, והטבילוה קודם לאמה משום מגע תרומה. עין בול ובית שערים מא"י, פומבדיתא חוץ לארץ:
Rashi on Niddah 32a:6:2.english: Before her mother - A woman who gives birth to a female immerses after fourteen [days], and her daughter saw [blood] one or two days after she was born, and they immersed her before her mother because of contact with terumah. Ein Bul and Beit She'arim are in Eretz Yisrael; Pumbedita is outside the Land [of Israel].

Rashi on Niddah 32a:7:1.english: Because of the teruma of Eretz Yisrael - For it is disqualified by touch.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:7:2.english: Emerges from his body - Such as a zav, a zavah, and a niddah.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:7:3.hebrew: והני מילי באכילה - כולה שמואל אמרה בבכורות בפ' הלוקח בהמה (דף כז.), ואפי' זב ונדה לא פסלי לה בנגיעה:
Rashi on Niddah 32a:7:3.english: And this applies to eating - Shmuel said the entirety of it in Bekhorot in the chapter [entitled] Halokeiach Behemah (page 27a), and even a zav and a niddah do not disqualify it through touch.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:8:1.hebrew: לסוכה שמן של תרומה - דסיכה כאכילה, ובאכילה קאמרינן דתרומת חו"ל אסורה לנדה:
Rashi on Niddah 32a:8:1.english: To anoint her with oil of terumah - For anointing is like eating, and with regard to eating we said that terumah of outside the Land is forbidden to a niddah.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:8:2.english: As it is taught - [To show] that anointing is like eating.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:8:3.english: And they shall not desecrate - [This verse] is written in the passage of the warning to ritually impure people regarding terumah.

Rashi on Niddah 32a:8:4.hebrew: לרבות את הסך - בכלל בקדשים לא יאכל עד אשר יטהר. שתיה בכלל אכילה, דכתיב (דברים י״ד:כ״ג) ואכלת מעשר דגנך וגו', תירוש חמרא הוא, וקרי ליה אכילה:
Rashi on Niddah 32a:8:4.english: To include one who anoints - [To be included] in the category of "Of the holy things he shall not eat until he is pure." Drinking is in the category of eating, as it is written (Deuteronomy 14:23): "And you shall eat the tithe of your grain [your wine, etc.]" — "tirosh" is wine, and [the verse] calls it "eating."

Rashi on Niddah 32a:9:1.english: And it came like water, etc. - [The verse] refers to the curse regarding the wicked person.

Tosafot on Niddah 32a:14:1.hebrew: אי גרס הלכתא הוא - א"ש, דלא הוי הלכתא אלא חדא. ומיהו, ברוב ספרים גרס ״נינהו״; היינו לפי שלא פירש רבא הי קרא והי הלכתא, כלומר אחד מן הפסוקים, וא"צ לפרש משום דקאי נמי אקרא דזכרים דלקמן. ובסוף הישן (סוכה דף כח.) גבי ״אזרח להוציא את הנשים״, קאמר ״הלכתא נינהו״, אע"ג דליכא אלא חדא:
Tosafot on Niddah 32a:14:1.english: If one reads: "It is a halakha" - It is well, for there is only one halakha. However, in most books the reading is "they [are halakhot]" (ninhu); this is because Rava did not specify which is [derived from] a verse and which is a halakha — that is to say, [which] one of the verses — and he did not need to specify, because it applies also to the verse regarding males below. And at the end of [the chapter entitled] HaYashen (Sukkah 28a), regarding "[the] homeborn" to exclude women, [the Gemara] says: "They are halakhot," even though there is only one.

Tosafot on Niddah 32a:1:1.hebrew: רבי מאיר היא - תימה, דמשמע דמתני' (לעיל נדה דף לא:) דבנות כותים נדות מעריסתן לא אתיא כרבנן, אלא כרבי מאיר דחייש למיעוטא וסבר דכותים גרי אמת הן, כדמוכח פ' שור שנגח ד' וה' (ב"ק לח:); אבל לרבנן דלא חיישי למיעוטא לא הוו נדות מעריסתן, ולא לר' יוסי, אע"ג דחייש למיעוטא בפרק אלמנה (יבמות דף סז:), כיון דקסבר כותים גרי אריות הן, כדמוכח במנחות בפרק רבי ישמעאל (מנחות דף סו:) דקאמר תורמין משל (ישראל) על של עובדי כוכבים, ואם כן כותים לא מטמאו בנדות, כדאמר לקמן: בנות ישראל מטמאין בזיבה ואין עובדי כוכבים מטמאים בזיבה. ותימה: והא בנות כותים דהוו נדות מעריסתן הוו מי"ח דבר, ובפ"ק דשבת (דף יג:) משמע דליכא מאן דפליג על י"ח דבר, ומשמע התם (דף יז:) דהוי מי"ח דבר לכ"ע! וי"ל, דאפי' רבנן דלא חיישי למיעוטא, ואפילו גרי אריות הן, שוינהו רבנן נדות מעריסתן, וגזרו עליהם טומאה כדי שלא יטמעו בהן, כמו שגזרו על בת עובד כוכבים. וא"ת: אם כן, אמאי מוקי לה כר"מ ומשום דחייש למיעוטא? לוקמיה ככ"ע ומשום טימוע! דר"מ נמי אית ליה טעמא דטימוע, דאמר בפ' ד' וה' (ב"ק דף לח:): קנסא דקניס ר"מ בממונא כדי שלא יטמעו בהן. וי"ל, משום דע"כ מתני' לית ליה טעמא דטימוע, אלא משום חשש ראיה, כדקתני: לפי שיושבות על כל דם ודם. והא דא"ר יוסי: מעשה בעין בול והטבילוה קודם לאמה — אע"ג דטעמא דרבי יוסי משום טימוע, הוצרך להביא ראיה דשכיח הוא שרואות הן בקטנותן, דאי לאו הכי הוי כחוכא וטלולא למיגזר בהן נדות. וא"ת: לר"מ דחייש למיעוטא וקסבר דכותים גרי אמת הן, א"כ הוו נדות מעריסתן מן התורה, ולמה מני לה מי"ח דבר? וי"ל, דמסתמא לא ראתה מיד אחר ההולדה רגע אחד, א"כ אוקמה בחזקת שלא ראתה, וסמוך רובא דלא חזו לחזקה שלא ראתה, והוו הנך דחזו מיעוטא דמיעוטא, ולא מטמו מדאורייתא, אלא מדרבנן הוא דגזרו עליהם מי"ח דבר. וא"ת: ולר' יוסי דגרי אריות הן, אמאי גזרו בכותים דהוו נדות מעריסתן, ובבת עובד כוכבים לא גזרו עד בת ג' שנים כדאמרינן התם? ויש לומר, דהחמירו בכותים דעבדי קצת מצות ולא בדילי ישראל מינייהו, וגזרו עליהם מעריסתן דלא ליתי וליטמעו בהן; אבל מעובדי כוכבים הוו בדילי טובא, ולא גזרו עלייהו עד דליהוי ראויות לביאה:
Tosafot on Niddah 32a:1:1.english: It is Rabbi Meir - It is astonishing, for [the Gemara] implies that our Mishnah (above, Niddah 31b) — that the daughters of Cutheans are niddot from their cradle — does not follow the Rabbis, but rather [follows only] Rabbi Meir, who takes a minority into account and holds that Cutheans are true converts (gerei emet), as is proven in the chapter [entitled] "Shor SheNagakh Arba'ah ve-Hamishah" (Bava Kamma 38b); but according to the Rabbis, who do not take a minority into account, they would not be niddot from their cradle; nor according to Rabbi Yosi, even though he takes a minority into account in the chapter [entitled] "Almanah" (Yevamot 67b), since he holds that Cutheans are "lion converts" (gerei arayot), as is proven in Menachot in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Yishmael" (Menachot 66b), where it says that one may separate terumah from that of (an Israelite) for that of gentiles; and if so, Cutheans do not become ritually impure through niddah, as [the Gemara] says below: "Daughters of Israel become impure through zivah, but gentile women do not become impure through zivah." And it is astonishing: for [the decree] that the daughters of Cutheans are niddot from their cradle was among the Eighteen Decrees, and in the first chapter of Shabbat (13b) it implies that there is no one who disputes the Eighteen Decrees, and it implies there (17b) that this is of the Eighteen Decrees according to all! And one can say that even according to the Rabbis, who do not take a minority into account, and even if they are lion converts, the Rabbis rendered them niddot from their cradle and decreed impurity upon them in order that [Israelites] should not assimilate among them, just as they decreed upon the daughter of a gentile. And if you say: If so, why does [the Gemara] establish [the Mishnah] in accordance with Rabbi Meir and because he takes a minority into account? Let it establish it in accordance with everyone, and because of assimilation! For Rabbi Meir also holds the reason of assimilation, as he said in the chapter [entitled] "Arba'ah ve-Hamishah" (Bava Kamma 38b): "[It is] a penalty that Rabbi Meir penalized regarding monetary matters in order that they should not assimilate among them." And one can say: Because perforce our Mishnah does not accept the reason of assimilation, but rather because of concern of seeing [blood], as it teaches: "Because they sit upon every blood." And as for that which Rabbi Yosi said: "An incident occurred in Ein Bul where they immersed her before her mother" — even though Rabbi Yosi's reason is because of assimilation, he was required to bring proof that it is common that they see [blood] in their childhood, for were it not so, it would be like a laughingstock and mockery to decree niddah upon them. And if you say: According to Rabbi Meir, who takes a minority into account and holds that Cutheans are true converts, if so, they would be niddot from their cradle by Torah law; why then does [the Gemara] count it among the Eighteen Decrees? And one can say: Ordinarily, [a newborn girl] did not see [blood] for one moment immediately after birth; if so, establish her upon the presumption that she has not seen [blood], and join the majority who do not see [blood] to the presumption that she has not seen, and those who do see become a minority of a minority; and [therefore] they do not become impure by Torah law, but rather it is by Rabbinic decree that they decreed upon them as one of the Eighteen Decrees. And if you say: And according to Rabbi Yosi, who holds that they are lion converts, why did they decree regarding Cutheans that they are niddot from their cradle, whereas regarding the daughter of a gentile they did not decree until [she is] three years old, as we say there? And one can say: They were more stringent regarding Cutheans, because they perform some mitzvot and Israelites do not keep separate from them, and [therefore] they decreed upon them from their cradle so that they would not come to assimilate among them; but from gentiles [Israelites] kept very separate, and so they did not decree upon them until they are fit for intercourse.

Tosafot on Niddah 32a:3:1.hebrew: שמא תמצא אילונית - וא"ת: ותתיבם ממה נפשך, דאם אילונית היא — הוי קידושי אחיו טעות, כדתנן (יבמות דף ב:): ״וכולן שנמצאו אילונית צרותיהן מותרות״, משום דלא הויא צרת ערוה. ותירץ ר"ת: דהכא איירי בדקבל עלויה אחיו; וכי האי גוונא משני בריש בן סורר ומורה (סנהדרין דף סט:), ואין להאריך כאן יותר. וא"ת: ובקטן אמאי חיישינן שמא ימצא סריס? וניבדקיה אם עושה כיפה כשמשתין או אחד משאר סימנין דאמר בהערל (יבמות דף פ:), ואיכא למ"ד התם דלא הוי סריס עד שיהו בו כל סימני סריס! וי"ל: דאין מועלת הבדיקה עד שהוא גדול בשנים:
Tosafot on Niddah 32a:3:1.english: Lest she be found [to be] an aylonit - And if you say: But let her enter into levirate marriage either way (mimah nafshekh)! For if she is an aylonit, his brother's betrothal was in error, as we learned in a Mishnah (Yevamot 2b): "And all of them who were found [to be] an aylonit, their co-wives are permitted," because she is not the co-wife of a forbidden relative (tzarat ervah). And Rabbeinu Tam answered that here we are dealing with [a case where] his brother accepted [her] upon himself; and in such a manner [the Gemara] answers at the beginning of [the chapter of] "Ben Sorer U-Moreh" (Sanhedrin 69b), and there is no need to elaborate here further. And if you say: And regarding a minor [boy], why do we suspect lest he be found [to be] a saris? But let us examine him [to see] if he forms an arch when he urinates, or [check for] one of the other signs that [the Gemara] states in [the chapter of] "Ha'arel" (Yevamot 80b) — and there is an authority there who holds that he is not a saris until all the signs of a saris are present in him! And one can say that the examination is not effective until he is grown in years.

Tosafot on Niddah 32a:6:1.hebrew: והטבילוה קודם לאמה - ומשום שראתה, דאי משום שנגעה באמה שטמאה לידה, א"כ, מאי אשמעינן? כל ולדות נמי טמאין. ובפרק עד כמה (בכורות דף כז'.) דקאמר גבי חלה דמאכילתו לכהן קטן, ה"ה לכהן גדול שטבל, כדמשמע הכא:
Tosafot on Niddah 32a:6:1.english: And they immersed her before her mother - And [this was] because she saw [blood], for if [it were] because she touched her mother who is impure due to childbirth, if so, what does this teach us? All newborns are also impure. And in the chapter [entitled] "Ad Kamma" (Bekhorot 27a), where it says regarding challah that one feeds it to a minor priest, the same applies to an adult priest who immersed, as is implied here.

Tosafot on Niddah 32a:9:1.hebrew: שתיה בכלל אכילה - וא"ת, בפרק העור והרוטב (חולין דף קכ.) גבי חלב, למה לי כל נפש לרבות שותה? ויש לומר, דאשמעינן דחלב מהותך שמיה חלב:
Tosafot on Niddah 32a:9:1.english: Drinking is included in [the category of] eating - And if you say: In the chapter [entitled] "Ha-Or Ve-ha-Rotev" (Chullin 120a), regarding forbidden fat (chelev), why do I need "any soul" (kol nefesh) to include one who drinks [it]? And one can say that it teaches us that melted fat is [still] considered fat.

Tosafot on Niddah 32a:9:2.hebrew: וכשמן בעצמותיו - ואם תאמר: דמעיקרא מייתי מן התורה, והדר מייתי אסמכתא — דבפרק ר"ע (שבת דף פו.) תנן: דסיכה ביוה"כ אסור, אע"ג שאין ראיה לדבר, זכר לדבר, שנאמר: ותבא כמים בקרבו? ואומר רבינו תם: דקרא דלא יחללו נמי אסמכתא הוא, דבפרק הנשרפין (סנהדרין דף פג.) דרשינן מיניה דטבל במיתה, ובפרק קמא דזבחים (דף ג:) מידרש לדרשא אחריתי; ומדאורייתא לא הוי סך כשותה, וכן לענין יוה"כ. ותדע: דאין חייבין כרת אלא אוכל ושותה בלבד; ואמר נמי בפרק בתרא דיומא (דף עז:): מי שיש לו חטטין בראשו, סך כדרכו ואינו חושש. ועוד אומר ר"ת: דדוקא סיכת שמן אסמכוה רבנן אקרא, ואסור מדרבנן; אבל סיכה של שומן חזיר ושל חלב — שריא. ובפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף כד:) אמר: המניח חלב של שור הנסקל ע"ג מכתו פטור, אבל אסור הוא, משום דאסור בהנאה — משמע: אבל חלב דעלמא, אפילו איסורא ליכא:
Tosafot on Niddah 32a:9:2.english: And like oil into his bones - And if you say: Initially [the Gemara] brings [a proof] from the Torah, and then it brings an asmachta (scriptural support) — for in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Akiva" (Shabbat 86a) we learned: Anointing on Yom Kippur is forbidden; even though there is no proof for the matter, [there is] a hint for the matter, as it is stated, "And it came into his innards like water [and like oil into his bones]"? And Rabbeinu Tam says that the verse "And they shall not desecrate" (Leviticus 22:15) is also an asmachta, for in the chapter [entitled] "HaNisrafin" (Sanhedrin 83a) we derive from it that [eating] tevel (untithed produce) is [punishable] by death [at the hand of Heaven], and in the first chapter of Zevachim (3b) it is expounded for another exposition; and by Torah law, anointing is not [equivalent to] drinking, and so too with regard to Yom Kippur. And know [that this is so], for one is liable to karet (spiritual excision) only [for] eating and drinking alone; and it was also said in the last chapter of Yoma (77b): "One who has scabs on his head may anoint in his usual manner and need not be concerned." And Rabbeinu Tam further says that specifically anointing with oil was supported by the Rabbis on the verse and is forbidden by rabbinic law, but anointing with swine fat or with forbidden fat (chelev) is permitted. And in the chapter [entitled] "Kol Sha'ah" (Pesachim 24b) it was said: "One who places the fat of an ox that is to be stoned upon his wound is exempt, but it is forbidden because it is forbidden from benefit" — which implies: but [with] ordinary forbidden fat, there is not even a prohibition.
